headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection and cascading-error from ChatGPT Desktop feeding mem0-style memory workflows; data leakage and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files, screenshots, clipboard, and app context, while mem0 is a memory layer that may store or reuse model outputs. That creates a plausible path where attacker-controlled content in A is later surfaced to B as trusted context. The pairwise bridge is documented only at the profile level, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop content is copied into mem0-backed memory without provenance labels
IF mem0 re-injects stored notes into later prompts or agent context
mitigations: Disable automatic memory writes from ChatGPT outputs
Add provenance tags to all imported notes
Review copied clipboard content before saving
Restrict mem0 to summaries, not raw transcripts
requires-engineering: add source-tracking on memory entries

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, but its egress is vendor-only; agent B shows no data classes touched and no network egress. With no shared workspace or authenticated principal shown, leakage is possible mainly through manual transfer of sensitive content, so the blast radius is limited and below medium.
conditions: IF sensitive files from ChatGPT Desktop are manually pasted into mem0
IF mem0 is configured to store raw transcripts containing uploaded-file contents
mitigations: Avoid pasting secrets into memory notes
Redact sensitive fields before import
Use separate accounts for A and B
Delete any accidental sensitive memory entries
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on imported text

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or use MCP, and mem0 exposes no write or coordination capabilities in the profile. Without overlapping mutable-resource writes, there is no plausible capability conflict pathway between the pair.
conditions: IF either profile gains shared write access to the same directory
IF mem0 is deployed with writable shared state not shown here
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only to shared resources
Avoid shared git worktrees
Do not mount a common writable folder
Document any future shared OAuth scopes
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable stores

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce code, screenshots, and file-derived claims; B is a knowledge-management layer that may reuse those outputs as memory. If B treats A's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into later prompts or decisions. Because B is not shown to verify provenance by default, medium is warranted rather than low.
conditions: IF mem0 stores ChatGPT-generated facts without verification
IF later prompts retrieve those facts as authoritative context
mitigations: Mark A outputs as unverified in memory
Require human review before saving facts
Store citations alongside each memory item
Purge stale or low-confidence memories
requires-engineering: add verification gates before recall

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, which can include regulated data, while mem0's profile shows no specific residency or retention commitments. The mismatch is therefore a documentation gap rather than a proven breach, and only one agent is directly implicated in the residency/retention concern.
conditions: IF regulated data from ChatGPT Desktop is stored in mem0 without a retention policy
IF the deployment requires GDPR or sector-specific residency controls
mitigations: Avoid storing regulated data in memory
Set a short retention window
Delete sensitive memories after use
Confirm vendor residency terms
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
